newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds, futures start well but soon lose spark.
newsitem.headline: Bunds, futures start well but soon lose spark.

text.p: German Bunds and futures started the session on a firmer note on Tuesday, pulling back slightly from Monday's weakness sparked by a swing to the left in the first round of French elections.
But within the first hour of trade, the June futures contract had returned to base and dipped into negative territory as EMU concerns continued to weigh.

By 0658 GMT, the DTB June contract was two basis points lower at 100.69, having been as high as 100.77 just after the open. The 10-year cash Bund held onto its firmer start, quoted at 100.51 for a 5.924 percent bid yield.
Analysts said the French political developments would prompt sympathy losses in Bunds if expectations for a right-wing victory at the next voting round on Sunday continue to wane.
But they said Bund weakness would be held in check by some flight-to-quality sentiment if Europe's currency union project appeared to be under threat.
"Just after international investors rated to underweight Germany recently, the potential flight into Deutschemarks on EMU concerns pops up," said analyst at DMG futures and options.
"This clearly limits the downside in the German market."
The technical picture for Bund futures, however, was not particularly supportive, analysts said.
"We're unlikely to get very far this session. The market is looking unsure and the 101.00 level will be tought to break through," said one trader.
On the downside, support for the June contract comes in at 100.63 and then in the 100.50 region.
The main data focus will be the April U.S. consumer confidence index due at 1400 GMT. Analysts polled by Reuters expect the index to ease back to 114.4 from 16.8 in March.
